question: In which place did Shah Mal lead the revolt in 1857?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Baraut**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sah Mal **was a **rebel **at the **time of the Indian Rebellion **of **1857.**
 
• It is **based out **of the **village of Bijrol**, **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• He **led **the **Jats of Baraut **in **rebellion **against the **East India Company**.
 
• **In June 1857**, **Sah Mal Singh **seized **500 head of cattle**, **collected **escaped convicts and **other locals, **and **formed a force**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• It **was **the **first expression **of **organised resistance **against the **British East India Company**.
 
• **It began **as a revolt of the **sepoys **of **the British East India Company’s army **but eventually **secured the participation of the masses**.
 
• The **revolt is **known by several names: **the Sepoy Mutiny **(by the British Historians), **the Indian Mutiny**, **the Great Rebellion **(by the Indian Historians),
 
• The **Revolt of 1857**, the **Indian Insurrection**, and **the First War of Independence **(by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar).
